title: Sales Enablement Playbook: Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pricing Guidance, Case Studies & Security FAQ
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Purpose

This playbook is the canonical sales enablement reference for Redwood Inference. It provides standardized positioning and messaging, short competitive briefs for rapid rebuttals, a recommended pitch-deck flow with talking points, pragmatic pricing guidance for early commercial discussions, reproducible case study templates and a concise security FAQ for prospect conversations. Use it to prepare AE/SE collateral, run pilots, and align cross-functional approvers.

Top-line positioning

One-liner
Redwood Inference: a developer-first inference platform that delivers predictable, cost-efficient, production-grade LLM serving across hosted, dedicated and private deployments.

Primary value pillars (for slide headers / opening emails)
- Production predictability: SLA-backed Dedicated capacity and runtime optimizations to meet latency SLOs.
- Cost efficiency: automatic batching, prefix/KV caching and model/quantization recommendations that reduce unit costs.
- Deployment choice: identical API and operational tooling across Hosted, Dedicated and Private modes.
- Reliability: smart routing, automated fallbacks and graceful degradation under pressure.
- Observability & control: token-level cost/latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards and rollout tooling.

Persona-specific messaging (one sentence each)
- Engineering Lead: Ship LLM features faster with fewer ops by using our runtime, SDKs and rollout controls.
- Platform/Infra: Guarantee capacity and isolation with Dedicated pools, autoscaling and RBAC integration.
- Product/PM: Maintain UX consistency and reduce regressions with built-in evals, AB tests and staged rollouts.
- Security/Compliance: Meet audit and key-management needs with VPC/private options, KMS/HSM and exportable evidence packages.

Common objections + one-line rebuttals
- "We can run open models ourselves": Hosting is one piece; production-grade serving requires optimized runtime, routing and observability which reduce long-term TCO.
- "Vendor lock-in": Redwood supports model/version pinning, standard APIs and Private deployments for customer-managed infrastructure.
- "Costs are unpredictable": Present unit economics examples, pilot telemetry and Optimize-driven cost-savings to demonstrate expected run-rate.

Competitive brief (one-page cheat-sheet)

Covered competitors: CloudA, MegaCloud AI, FastLLM, ChatServe, SelfServeRuntime.
Key decision axes: latency SLOs, steady-state cost per token, deployment flexibility, observability/ops tooling, security/compliance readiness.

Short competitor positions
- Redwood Inference: Strong on performance predictability, cost controls and unified tooling across deployment modes; best suited for teams prioritizing production economics and operational visibility.
- CloudA / MegaCloud AI: Excellent cloud integration and ecosystem fit; may cost more at sustained throughput and have multi-tenant variability.
- FastLLM / ChatServe: Good developer UX and model breadth; weaker enterprise SLAs and private deployment support.
- SelfServeRuntime: Lowest vendor spend for teams that can operate heavy infra; higher engineering maintenance and slower time-to-market.

Quick rebuttal bullets for AE/SEs
- CloudA: Emphasize Dedicated SLAs, routing/fallbacks and per-token efficiency at scale.
- FastLLM: Emphasize enterprise features, Private deployments and Optimize toolkit.
- Self-hosting: Emphasize total cost of ownership (engineering time, incident risk, and slower iteration).

Pitch deck: recommended flow and talking points

10-12 slide recommended order (concise)
1) Title + one-liner
2) Customer pain: examples of latency/cost/reliability problems
3) Redwood solution summary (hosted/dedicated/private)
4) Architecture overview: runtime, compilation/kernels, routing and caching
5) Performance: sample SLOs and benchmark highlights (median latency, p95, throughput)
6) Cost story: how batching/caching/quantization cut unit spend with example math
7) Deployment & security: VPC, KMS integrations, audit logs and deployment options
8) Case study (1): configuration and measurable outcomes
9) Pilot plan: timeline, success metrics and SE involvement
10) Commercial snapshot: pricing ranges and contract options
11) Appendix/next steps: contacts and technical appendix

Slide guidance
- Keep top 3 slides tailored to persona. Each slide: 1-1 value sentence + 2-3 supporting bullets (metrics, timelines, ownership). Include appendix with API examples, benchmark methodology and sample SLOs.

Pricing guidance (how to discuss ranges)

Pricing models summary
- Hosted: usage-based (input/output tokens, embeddings).
- Dedicated: monthly/annual reserved GPU capacity with committed throughput and overage rules.
- Private: license + annual support and deployment services.
- Add-ons: higher observability retention, compliance packages, premium SLA.

Ballpark ranges for early conversations (confirm with finance for quotes)
- Hosted API: $0.0008-0.02 per output token (model-dependent). Embeddings: $0.0003-0.004 per vector.
- Dedicated: entry-level ~ $25k/month; mid-market $75k-100k+/month depending on GPU class and commit.
- Private: example small deployment ~ $150k license + $50k/year support; larger on-prem deals vary significantly.

Deal structuring & concession rules
1) Pilot offers: time-bound credits + 30-60 day SE-led POC with defined success metrics.
2) Procurement pushback: staged commit (e.g., 6 then 12 months) and downgrade paths to Hosted.
3) Price-sensitive buyers: propose technical pilot showing Optimize improvements (quantization + caching) before long-term commit.
4) Discount approvals: finance must approve >20% discounts or non-standard payment terms.

Case studies: template + two examples

Template (use for all stories)
- Customer: name and vertical
- Problem: scale/latency/cost or compliance challenge
- Redwood solution: deployment mode, model variant, runtime optimizations and rollout plan
- Outcome: numeric before/after metrics and business impact
- Reference contact: if available

NovaDocs (SaaS document automation)
- Problem: High per-call costs and inconsistent latency causing churn among high-volume enterprise customers.
- Solution: Dedicated GPU pools, prefix/KV chat caching, and FP16 quantized model path for best-effort responses.
- Outcome: median latency down from 450ms to 150ms, ~38% per-token cost reduction, top-10 customer deployment in 8 weeks.

BrightHealth (Healthcare triage assistant, private deployment)
- Problem: PHI-sensitive workflows required on-prem deployment and customer-managed keys; previous projects had long ops lead times.
- Solution: Private on-prem package, KMS integration, hardened network config and SE-assisted deployment.
- Outcome: 6-week deployment, SOC-ready logs, 12% improvement in triage accuracy and signed multi-year contract.

Security FAQ (short answers for AE/SEs)

Q: Where is customer data stored?
A: Hosted: data stored in Redwood-managed encrypted stores with configurable retention. Private: data remains in customer VPC/on-prem. KMS/HSM integrations available.

Q: Can Redwood be deployed in our VPC/on-prem?
A: Yes. Redwood Private supports VPC-hosted control plane patterns and a packaged on-prem offering; SE engagements available for initial hardening.

Q: What certifications / evidence do you provide?
A: We can provide SOC/ISO artifacts where applicable and offer customized evidence packages for enterprise customers under NDA.

Q: How is access controlled?
A: RBAC for Console/API, SSO via SAML/OIDC for Dedicated/Private, and audit trails for role changes and rollouts.

Q: Are model weights and keys protected?
A: For Private, model artifacts can be stored in customer-managed buckets. Keys integrate with KMS/HSM. All network traffic uses TLS 1.2+ by default.

Q: What logging and audit capabilities exist?
A: Token-level metrics, API access logs, rollout/audit trails and configurable retention. Export hooks to SIEMs are supported.

Q: How to mitigate data leakage/prompt extraction?
A: Combine technical controls (response filtering, redaction, rate limits), policy controls (PII detection) and private deployments. Our Quality Guardrails team can run evals on canonical prompts.
